links.outcome: Effect of leakage-free versus split-after-augmentation evaluation on apparent AUC gains from synthetic augmentation
links.effect: Gains attributed to augmentation are largely leakage artifacts, contributing up to +0.17 AUC in multiclass settings; no augmentation method improved on the unaugmented baseline (best AUC 0.838-0.842).
links.quote: Gains commonly attributed to augmentation are, to a large extent, an artifact of evaluation leakage, contributing up to +0.17 AUC in multiclass settings.

unlisted_practices: Decomposing apparent augmentation gains into baseline, genuine augmentation, and leakage terms
Assessing synthetic-sample fidelity with classifier two-sample test, Wasserstein distance, and distance-to-closest-record
Latent-space versus raw-space class balancing order for multimodal synthetic augmentation

screen.reason: The paper investigates methodological validation artifacts (data leakage from synthetic data augmentation) in a multimodal Parkinson's disease classification benchmark, rather than testing a clinical deployment practice or safeguard.
